Swim Seattle

A Water Safety and Equity Initiative

Swim Seattle Logo

The Swim Seattle initiative combines the efforts of Seattle Parks & Recreation, YMCA, No More Under, Associated Recreation Council, and other drowning prevention partners. The goal of Swim Seattle is to remove barriers to swimming opportunities, centering the communities who need it the most.

Swim Seattle - A Drowning Prevention and Youth Aquatics Initiative from Seattle Parks and Recreation on Vimeo.

What is Swim Seattle?

Free Swim Lessons & Early Registration 

Free Teen Swims

  • Several pools offer a free weekly teen swim. 
  • Teen swims include open swim time, swim instruction, and pre-lifeguard training.
  • Please check with your local pool for schedule.

Community Trainings, Events and Partnerships

  • We host Water Safety Days, life jacket and swim gear giveaways, culturally inclusive workshops and trainings, awareness campaigns, and more.
  • Check out Swim Seattle on the Parkways blog for upcoming events.

A lifeguard in the water holds hands with two young girls learning to swim with kickboards

Swim Lessons through our Community Partners

You may be looking for classes that have space open, or for additional locations.  Contact these community partners:

Seattle Parks Swim Beaches offer free swimming lessons to all children age 6-16 during summer 2024.  Details on the swim beaches page.  Register via email instead of through Active Net.  Children receiving free Swim Seattle lessons may also participate in free swim beach lessons!

The YMCA of Greater Seattle offers free lessons for scholarship-eligible participants.

No More Under offers free swim lessons to specific communities.

([Ballard](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/ballard-pool), [Colman](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/colman-pool), [Mounger](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/mounger-pool), [Rainier Beach](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool)) | | $1.00 | | Coin Operated Locker | | $0.25 | | Towel Rental (Most sites) | | $0.50 | ## Swim Program Descriptions Below are general descriptions of swim programs offered across the Seattle Parks and Recreation pool system. Some locations may have variations, so please check with each pool for specific details. ## Recreation Swims ### Adult & Senior Swim Adult Swim is time set aside for recreational swimming for adults 18 or older. We set aside one part of the pool for lap swimming and leave the rest of the pool available for less structured swimming. ### Family Swim Family Swim is a Recreation Swim with slightly different rules to foster a somewhat quieter mood: - Children younger than 18 must be accompanied into the pool by a responsible adult. - Children younger than 6 years of age or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult who is within an arm's length at all times. ### Recreation Swim Recreation Swim is a full- or half-pool recreation time for swimmers of all ages. - Children younger than 6 or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult within arm's reach at all times. - Swimmers younger than 18 years must pass a swim test before using the deep end. - Deep water attractions may be in use: diving boards, rope swings, and water slides depending on location. - Personal Flotation Devices are available to borrow. ### Lap Swim Lap Swim is a continuous lap swim for swimmers of all ages; we divide the lanes according to speed levels. ### Early Morning Lap Swim - Exact Change or Quick Card required Early Morning Lap Swim is a great opportunity for early morning swimmers. It's for lap swimmers of all ages; we set up lanes according to speed levels. You'll need a pre-purchased swim card for entry. ## Fitness Swims ### Adult Drop In Swim Clinic Drop-In Adult Swim Stroke Clinic. Feedback provided by Red Cross Water Safety Instructors. Must have intermediate swimming ability (able to back float and comfortable in deep water). **Additional details:** Age: 16 or older Fee: Fitness Program fee applies Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ### Deep Water Exercise Deep Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a non-impact environment. Participants should be comfortable in deep water where they cannot touch the bottom. Flotation belts are provided. Deep Water Exercise incorporates aerobic conditioning, muscular strengthening, and abdominal toning. Provided resistance equipment may include dumbbell buoys and water noodles, or even just your open hands. Deep Water Exercise is often considered more advanced than Shallow Water Exercise; however, most Deep Water participants still find Shallow Water Exercise to be valuable!  ### Shallow Water Exercise Shallow Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a low-impact environment. No swimming ability is required. We recommend exercising in chest-deep water. Exercises include aerobics, strength and toning, and abdominal work.  Provided equipment may include dumbbell buoys or water noodles.  Thanks to support from the pool floor, Shallow Water Exercise may be well suited for those who want to work on balance, as well as those who may be recovering from joint injuries.*  *This is not medical advice. Please consult a qualified physician before beginning a new exercise program. ### Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout) Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout) is a structured workout led by experienced instructors designed to help you get in shape, stay in shape, or prepare for an important swim meet. Workouts are for adults 18 and older. ### Jr. Masters Jr. Masters is a drop-in competitive level coached swim for youth age 7-16 years old.  Youth should know the 4 competitive strokes and be able to swim at least 200 yards at a time. ## Special Aquatics Programs ### Adult Beginner Water Polo ($12) Adult water polo program suitable for beginners and anyone else interested in working on water polo basics in a fun environment. Topics will include strategies for passing, guarding and shooting, and each session will include a short scrimmage. To fully participate, we recommend that you feel comfortable: - Treading water for a minute with hands out of the water - Swimming 100 yards freestyle with head up **Additional details:** Age: 16 or older Fee: $12 a session Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ### Aqua Zumba Enjoy the lighter load on your joints as you dance to the Latin beats of salsa, reggaeton, merengue, and cumbia! Aqua Zumba is a fun twist on Shallow Water Exercise: a 45-minute, all-cardio, all-dance party led by a licensed Zumba and Aqua Zumba instructor. No swimming ability required. To account for water resistance, moves are timed more slowly than a traditional land-based Zumba class.  **Additional details:** Age: Adults, age 18+. Cost: Fitness Admission fees apply. Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ### Women's Only Swim (Rainier Beach only) Seattle Parks and Recreation is proud to offer single gender public swim and swimming lessons for women who, because of cultural or personal reasons, cannot swim in a co-ed environment. During these programs the windows to the pool are covered and only female instructors are employed for privacy. **Additional details:** Age: All ages. Cost: Recreation Admission fees apply. Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ### Lifeguard Jobs ## Lifeguard Jobs ## Current Aquatics Openings - **[Lifeguard (Temporary, Intermittent)](https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/seattle/jobs/5269368/lifeguard-temporary-intermittent?department%5B0%5D=Seattle%20Parks%20%26%20Recreation%20Department&sort=PositionTitle%7CAscending&pagetype=jobOpportunitiesJobs "Lifeguard Temp 2026").  Closes June 16, 2026.**  Work at swimming beaches, outdoor swimming pools, or indoor swimming pools. Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round. Visit at [any swimming pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools) to get started, even when no posting is active. ## How to Apply 1. **Get Certified!** Sign up for an American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course. 2. **Get Hired**! Three options: 1. Apply online on Government Jobs, if a listing is active. 2. Send an [Aquatic Application](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/Aquatic%20Application_ADA.pdf), or resume and cover letter, to [parksaquatics@seattle.gov](mailto:parksaquatics@seattle.gov). ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.*** 3. Take your application directly to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle Parks and Recreation indoor pool. ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.*** 3. **Get Working!** Once you are hired you will be required to pass a background check and a physical examination provided by the City of Seattle, as well as take the [NW Lifeguard Test](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool#NWLifeguardTest). For more information please call [(206) 684-4078](). ## Aquatics Certifications ### Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED (American Red Cross) ## Lifeguard Training Certification All City of Seattle lifeguards must have an active **American Red Cross certification in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED.** The 30-hour blended learning course includes both online and in-person components. Completion of the course grants initial certifications in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED. **Certifications are valid for 2 years.** [Find Blended Learning - Lifeguard courses.](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20blended&viewMode=list) ### Prerequisites: - At least 15 years old on or before the final scheduled session of the course. - Swim 150 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both, maintain position at the surface of the water for 2 minutes by treading water using only the legs, then swim an additional 50 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both. Swimming on the back or side is not allowed. Swim goggles may be used. Candidates should place their hands under the armpits for the treading water portion. - Complete a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds.  Starting in the water, swim 20 yards, dive 7-10 feet to retrieve a 10 pound object, swim 20 yards on the back to return to the starting point and exit the water without using a ladder.  Swim goggles may *not* be used. --- ## Lifeguard Renewal (recertification) **Lifeguard Renewal** is a one-day course for those who have a current certification, or one that has expired in the last 30 days. It will extend the expiration date of your Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED certifications for another 2 years. [Find Lifeguard Renewal courses](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20renewal&viewMode=list) To ask about planned Lifeguard Renewal course dates later than those currently listed in our registration system, please email [parksaquatics@seattle.gov](mailto:parksaquatics@seattle.gov). ### Northwest Lifeguard Test ## Northwest Lifeguard Test The Northwest Lifeguard Test (NWLGT) is a test of swimming ability and lifeguarding skills. The test builds on skills learned in the Red Cross lifeguarding course. It is meant to be taken after completing the Red Cross lifeguarding course, and is not a substitute for Red Cross lifeguard certification. NWLGT is offered about once a month and must be taken prior to working your first shift (for permanent positions, you will have 90 days from date of hire). The test is sponsored by Seattle Parks and Recreation, King County Parks, and the City of Covington. Test elements include: 1. 50 yards head high crawl stroke* 2. Rescue tow medley and underwater swim* 3. Spinal injury rescue in shallow water 4. Submerged victim recovery and CPR 5. Rescue of struggling victim [Grading Criteria](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/NW%20test%20grading%20criteria.pdf) *There are two levels of NW Test certification. The full/beach certification, and modified/indoor pool certification. The time of the Head High 50 Yard Swim and number of breaths taken on the Underwater Swim in the Medley will determine your certification level. See Grading Criteria or call your nearest pool for details. #### 2026 Northwest Lifeguard Test Dates 1. **Sat, Feb. 7**, 1pm-5pm at [Ballard Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/ballard-pool) 2. **Sun, Mar. 8**, 8am-12pm at [Southwest Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/southwest-pool) 3. **Sat, Apr. 4**, 1pm-5pm at [Helene Madison Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/helene-madison-pool) 4. **Sun, May 3**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 5. **Sun, May 17**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 6. **Sun, June 7**, 8am-12pm at [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) 7. **Sat, June 13**, 1pm-5pm at [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) 8. **Sun, July 12**, 8am-12pm at [Meadowbrook Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/meadowbrook-pool) 9. **Sun, Aug. 16**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 10. **Sun, Nov. 15,** 8am-12pm at [Southwest Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/southwest-pool) [Register for Northwest Lifeguard Test](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?activity_keyword=northwest%20lifeguard%20test&viewMode=list) ### FREE Lifeguard Training Team (LTT) The Lifeguard Training Team is a **FREE** summer program designed to train and certify Seattle's youth in lifesaving skills. **The eight week program for youth ages 15-18** will train participants to be lifeguards and build other important job skills. Seattle Parks and Recreation provides training, books, uniforms, and basic materials at no charge. LTT participants bring their own towels, swimsuits, goggles, and snacks. The Lifeguard Training Team includes a full American Red Cross lifeguard training course, and much more! Participants get the opportunity to test for certification at the end of the program. The Lifeguard Training Team is a tremendous opportunity for you to learn and grow, to build lasting friendships, and to acquire skills you'll use for the rest of your life. You don't have to be an Olympic athlete or world class swimmer to join. We just ask that you try your hardest, participate every day, and be part of the team. The instructors' provide a safe, well supervised and encouraging environment. The safety of the participants is our #1 priority. ### 2026 LTT Program Information 50 participants max, 25 at each location. Full attendance is mandatory. Participants must pass the lifeguard pre-test. Early registration is encouraged as LTT fills on a first-come, first served basis.  June 29 - August 20, 2026. Monday - Thursday, 1pm - 5pm South location: Pritchard Beach, [8400 55th Ave S, 98118](https://www.google.com/maps/place/8400+55th+Ave+S,+Seattle,+WA+98118/@47.5298267,-122.266172,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x5490420a71f550e9:0x54145e7fa1ceb76b!8m2!3d47.5298231!4d-122.2635971!16s%2Fg%2F11cnd8q08l!5m1!1e1?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDQxNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) North location: West Green Lake Beach [7312 W Green Lake Dr N, 98103](https://www.google.com/maps/place/7312+West+Green+Lake+Dr+N,+Seattle,+WA+98103/@47.6821168,-122.3423875,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x54901415e801e2b5:0xb88d5214d8912e10!8m2!3d47.6821132!4d-122.3398126!16s%2Fg%2F11c3q4947v!5m1!1e1?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDQxNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) ### Participant Swimming Skills Pre-Test Each participant must attend a swimming skills pre-tests before the first class. The pre-test is a prerequisite for the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training Course. It is also your chance to meet the instructors and ask questions about the program. Please bring a swimsuit and towel and be prepared to swim. **Pre-tests will take place at indoor pools in June, and take about 1 hour.** Specific date and location options will be provided when applications are accepted. ### Prerequisites: - Swim 150 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both, maintain position at the surface of the water for 2 minutes by treading water using only the legs, then swim an additional 50 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both. Swimming on the back or side is not allowed. Swim goggles may be used. Candidates should place their hands under the armpits for the treading water portion. - Complete a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds.  Starting in the water, swim 20 yards, dive 7-10 feet to retrieve a 10 pound object, swim 20 yards on the back to return to the starting point and exit the water without using a ladder.  Swim goggles may *not* be used. [Apply for the Lifeguard Training Team!](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=RR7meOtrCUCPmTWdi1T0G_X1kIYNvm9AinyqLpWJsfRUME03UUJHSVNYN01KVUhJVkJHQVI5QVc1VS4u) ### Sr. Lifeguard: Water Safety Instructor, Lifeguard Instructor ## Water Safety Instructor (WSI) Senior Lifeguards are required to hold a [Water Safety Instructor](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/swimming/water-safety/water-safety-instructor-certification) certification from the American Red Cross.  The certification may be attained within 90 days of hire. ## Lifeguard Instructor (LGI) This approximately 30 hour course includes practical methods and theory for teaching lifeguarding skills. Candidates must have a current Red Cross certification in Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED. LGI-certified instructors can certify in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED. Completion of this course also extends your Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED certifications for 2 years. Lifeguard Instructor is a highly desired, but optional certification for Senior Lifeguards. LGI is required for Assistant Aquatic Center Coordinator and Aquatic Center Coordinator positions. ## Amenities - ADA Lift - Portable Access Stairs - Water Slide - Spa/warm pool - Sauna - Family changing rooms - 1 M Diving Board ## Images The following photo gallery contains images related to this facility/park ## About We are one of eight indoor pools operated by Seattle Parks and Recreation. Located on Rainier Avenue S, we offer a wide array of aquatics programs for all ages. Our lessons offerings include tot lessons (6 months to 4 years of age), kinder lessons, youth lessons, youth competitive stroke lessons, adult and senior adult lessons, and private lessons. Exercise classes include aqua jogging, hydro-fit exercise, and water exercise. We also offer family swim, public swim, and lap swim times. ## Slide Swim Test and Rules Children under 48" (4ft in height) must pass a swim test in order to use the slide.  Lifejackets cannot be worn on the slide.  Two people cannot go down the slide together (this includes a parent and child).  Children cannot be caught by parents at the bottom of the slide. An adult must accompany children who do not meet age and height requirements. One adult may supervise only two children at a time.  Adults must remain within arm's reach of supervised children. Children under 48" (4ft in height) OR younger than six years of age must be accompanied in the water by a paying adult. Child must fulfill both height and age requirements to be able to swim without an adult. ## Related Links - **[Fees & Swim Descriptions](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/fees-and-programs)** - **[Purchase a Swim Pass](https://apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/Membership)** - **[Aquatics Jobs](https://www.seattle.gov/parks/about-us/jobs/aquatics-employment-and-training)** ## **Free & Low Cost Programs** - **[Free Hygiene Shower Locations](https://parkways.seattle.gov/2020/03/16/seattle-parks-and-recreations-free-shower-program-operating-on-modified-schedule-at-5-community-centers/)** - [**Swim Seattle (Scholarship Lessons)**](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/swim-seattle "Swim Seattle Initiative") - **[Financial Aid Application](https://seattle.gov/parks/scholarships-and-financial-aid)** ## Sign Up for Activities Here See what programs and activities you can sign up for right now at Rainier Beach pool and community center. ## Rental Policies - Indoor Pools

### Reserving a Rental Time

To reserve a rental time, please call the swimming pool you would like to reserve.  Some pools process reservations in-person only. Payment is due at the time of reservation.

Rentals are generally available on weekends after the conclusion of the final public drop-in program. Rental availability varies by location. Availability can be checked by calling the pool by phone.

### Pool Rules

- Alcohol, recreational drugs, and smoking are prohibited. Guests who appear intoxicated will not be permitted to swim or supervise children.
- Food is allowed, but glass containers are prohibited.
- Small sound systems are allowed. Tables and chairs are available.
- Deep water attractions are open to swimmers who pass the deep water swim test without the use of a Personal Flotation Device (PFD). Deep water attractions vary by pool and may include diving boards, rope swings, or water slides.
- Children younger than 6 years of age or shorter than 4 feet in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult who is always within an arm’s length away. Any child under this age or height requirement needs to be accompanied by an adult on a 2 children per 1 adult ratio.
- Children who pass the swim test may swim further from their adult (outside of arm’s reach) and use deep water attractions. An adult is still required to swim with the child.
- We recommend that you inform all parents if your party attendees may be under the age or height requirement, so parents can be prepared to get into the pool.
- Swim diapers are required for swimmers who are not toilet trained. Diapers must be changed in the locker rooms.
- The lifeguard on duty is the final authority on safety rules.

## Swim Program Descriptions

Below are general descriptions of swim programs offered across the Seattle Parks and Recreation pool system. Some locations may have variations, so please check with each pool for specific details.

## Recreation Swims

## Adult & Senior Swim

Adult Swim is time set aside for recreational swimming for adults 18 or older. We set aside one part of the pool for lap swimming and leave the rest of the pool available for less structured swimming.

## Family Swim

Family Swim is a Recreation Swim with slightly different rules to foster a somewhat quieter mood:

- Children younger than 18 must be accompanied into the pool by a responsible adult.
- Children younger than 6 years of age or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult who is within an arm's length at all times.

## Recreation Swim

Recreation Swim is a full- or half-pool recreation time for swimmers of all ages.

- Children younger than 6 or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult within arm's reach at all times.
- Swimmers younger than 18 years must pass a swim test before using the deep end.
- Deep water attractions may be in use: diving boards, rope swings, and water slides depending on location.
- Personal Flotation Devices are available to borrow.

## Lap Swim

Lap Swim is a continuous lap swim for swimmers of all ages; we divide the lanes according to speed levels.

## Early Morning Lap Swim - Exact Change or Quick Card required

Early Morning Lap Swim is a great opportunity for early morning swimmers. It's for lap swimmers of all ages; we set up lanes according to speed levels. You'll need a pre-purchased swim card for entry.

## Fitness Swims

## Adult Drop In Swim Clinic

Drop-In Adult Swim Stroke Clinic. Feedback provided by Red Cross Water Safety Instructors. Must have intermediate swimming ability (able to back float and comfortable in deep water).

**Additional details:**

Age: 16 or older  
Fee: Fitness Program fee applies  
Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool)

## Deep Water Exercise

Deep Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a non-impact environment. Participants should be comfortable in deep water where they cannot touch the bottom. Flotation belts are provided.

Deep Water Exercise incorporates aerobic conditioning, muscular strengthening, and abdominal toning. Provided resistance equipment may include dumbbell buoys and water noodles, or even just your open hands.

Deep Water Exercise is often considered more advanced than Shallow Water Exercise; however, most Deep Water participants still find Shallow Water Exercise to be valuable! 

## Shallow Water Exercise

Shallow Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a low-impact environment. No swimming ability is required. We recommend exercising in chest-deep water.

Exercises include aerobics, strength and toning, and abdominal work.  Provided equipment may include dumbbell buoys or water noodles. 

Thanks to support from the pool floor, Shallow Water Exercise may be well suited for those who want to work on balance, as well as those who may be recovering from joint injuries.* 

*This is not medical advice. Please consult a qualified physician before beginning a new exercise program.

## Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout)

Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout) is a structured workout led by experienced instructors designed to help you get in shape, stay in shape, or prepare for an important swim meet. Workouts are for adults 18 and older.

## Jr. Masters

Jr. Masters is a drop-in competitive level coached swim for youth age 7-16 years old.  Youth should know the 4 competitive strokes and be able to swim at least 200 yards at a time.

## Special Aquatics Programs

## Adult Beginner Water Polo ($12)

Adult water polo program suitable for beginners and anyone else interested in working on water polo basics in a fun environment.

Topics will include strategies for passing, guarding and shooting, and each session will include a short scrimmage.

To fully participate, we recommend that you feel comfortable:

- Treading water for a minute with hands out of the water
- Swimming 100 yards freestyle with head up

**Additional details:**

Age: 16 or older  
Fee: $12 a session  
Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool)

## Aqua Zumba

Enjoy the lighter load on your joints as you dance to the Latin beats of salsa, reggaeton, merengue, and cumbia!

Aqua Zumba is a fun twist on Shallow Water Exercise: a 45-minute, all-cardio, all-dance party led by a licensed Zumba and Aqua Zumba instructor. No swimming ability required.

To account for water resistance, moves are timed more slowly than a traditional land-based Zumba class. 

**Additional details:**

Age: Adults, age 18+.  
Cost: Fitness Admission fees apply.  
Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool)

## Women's Only Swim (Rainier Beach only)

Seattle Parks and Recreation is proud to offer single gender public swim and swimming lessons for women who, because of cultural or personal reasons, cannot swim in a co-ed environment.

During these programs the windows to the pool are covered and only female instructors are employed for privacy.

**Additional details:**

Age: All ages.  
Cost: Recreation Admission fees apply.  
Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool)

## How to Apply

1. **Get Certified!** Sign up for an American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course.
2. **Get Hired**! Three options:
   
   1. Apply online on Government Jobs, if a listing is active.
   2. Send an [Aquatic Application](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/Aquatic%20Application_ADA.pdf), or resume and cover letter, to parksaquatics@seattle.gov. ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.***
   3. Take your application directly to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle Parks and Recreation indoor pool. ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.***
3. **Get Working!** Once you are hired you will be required to pass a background check and a physical examination provided by the City of Seattle, as well as take the [NW Lifeguard Test](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/ballard-pool#NWLifeguardTest).

For more information please call (206) 684-4078.

## Aquatics Certifications

## Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED (American Red Cross)

## Lifeguard Training Certification

All City of Seattle lifeguards must have an active **American Red Cross certification in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED.**

The 30-hour blended learning course includes both online and in-person components. Completion of the course grants initial certifications in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED. **Certifications are valid for 2 years.**

[Find Blended Learning - Lifeguard courses.](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20blended&viewMode=list)

### Prerequisites:

- At least 15 years old on or before the final scheduled session of the course.
- Swim 150 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both, maintain position at the surface of the water for 2 minutes by treading water using only the legs, then swim an additional 50 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both. Swimming on the back or side is not allowed. Swim goggles may be used. Candidates should place their hands under the armpits for the treading water portion.
- Complete a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds.  Starting in the water, swim 20 yards, dive 7-10 feet to retrieve a 10 pound object, swim 20 yards on the back to return to the starting point and exit the water without using a ladder.  Swim goggles may *not* be used.

* * *

## Lifeguard Renewal (recertification)

**Lifeguard Renewal** is a one-day course for those who have a current certification, or one that has expired in the last 30 days. It will extend the expiration date of your Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED certifications for another 2 years.

[Find Lifeguard Renewal courses](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20renewal&viewMode=list)

To ask about planned Lifeguard Renewal course dates later than those currently listed in our registration system, please email parksaquatics@seattle.gov.

## Northwest Lifeguard Test

## Northwest Lifeguard Test

The Northwest Lifeguard Test (NWLGT) is a test of swimming ability and lifeguarding skills. The test builds on skills learned in the Red Cross lifeguarding course. It is meant to be taken after completing the Red Cross lifeguarding course, and is not a substitute for Red Cross lifeguard certification.

NWLGT is offered about once a month and must be taken prior to working your first shift (for permanent positions, you will have 90 days from date of hire).

The test is sponsored by Seattle Parks and Recreation, King County Parks, and the City of Covington.

Test elements include:

1. 50 yards head high crawl stroke*
2. Rescue tow medley and underwater swim*
3. Spinal injury rescue in shallow water
4. Submerged victim recovery and CPR
5. Rescue of struggling victim

[Grading Criteria](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/NW%20test%20grading%20criteria.pdf)

*There are two levels of NW Test certification. The full/beach certification, and modified/indoor pool certification. The time of the Head High 50 Yard Swim and number of breaths taken on the Underwater Swim in the Medley will determine your certification level. See Grading Criteria or call your nearest pool for details.

## FREE Lifeguard Training Team (LTT)

 

The Lifeguard Training Team is a **FREE** summer program designed to train and certify Seattle's youth in lifesaving skills. **The eight week program for youth ages 15-18** will train participants to be lifeguards and build other important job skills.

Seattle Parks and Recreation provides training, books, uniforms, and basic materials at no charge. LTT participants bring their own towels, swimsuits, goggles, and snacks. The Lifeguard Training Team includes a full American Red Cross lifeguard training course, and much more! Participants get the opportunity to test for certification at the end of the program.

The Lifeguard Training Team is a tremendous opportunity for you to learn and grow, to build lasting friendships, and to acquire skills you'll use for the rest of your life. You don't have to be an Olympic athlete or world class swimmer to join. We just ask that you try your hardest, participate every day, and be part of the team. The instructors' provide a safe, well supervised and encouraging environment. The safety of the participants is our #1 priority.

### Participant Swimming Skills Pre-Test

Each participant must attend a swimming skills pre-tests before the first class. The pre-test is a prerequisite for the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training Course. It is also your chance to meet the instructors and ask questions about the program.

Please bring a swimsuit and towel and be prepared to swim. **Pre-tests will take place at indoor pools in June, and take about 1 hour.** Specific date and location options will be provided when applications are accepted.

### Prerequisites:

- Swim 150 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both, maintain position at the surface of the water for 2 minutes by treading water using only the legs, then swim an additional 50 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both. Swimming on the back or side is not allowed. Swim goggles may be used. Candidates should place their hands under the armpits for the treading water portion.
- Complete a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds.  Starting in the water, swim 20 yards, dive 7-10 feet to retrieve a 10 pound object, swim 20 yards on the back to return to the starting point and exit the water without using a ladder.  Swim goggles may *not* be used.

## Sr. Lifeguard: Water Safety Instructor, Lifeguard Instructor

## Water Safety Instructor (WSI)

Senior Lifeguards are required to hold a [Water Safety Instructor](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/swimming/water-safety/water-safety-instructor-certification) certification from the American Red Cross.  The certification may be attained within 90 days of hire.

## Lifeguard Instructor (LGI)

This approximately 30 hour course includes practical methods and theory for teaching lifeguarding skills. Candidates must have a current Red Cross certification in Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED. LGI-certified instructors can certify in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED. Completion of this course also extends your Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED certifications for 2 years.

Lifeguard Instructor is a highly desired, but optional certification for Senior Lifeguards. LGI is required for Assistant Aquatic Center Coordinator and Aquatic Center Coordinator positions.

Some locations may have variations, so please check with each pool for specific details. ## Recreation Swims ### Adult & Senior Swim Adult Swim is time set aside for recreational swimming for adults 18 or older. We set aside one part of the pool for lap swimming and leave the rest of the pool available for less structured swimming. ### Family Swim Family Swim is a Recreation Swim with slightly different rules to foster a somewhat quieter mood: - Children younger than 18 must be accompanied into the pool by a responsible adult. - Children younger than 6 years of age or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult who is within an arm's length at all times. ### Recreation Swim Recreation Swim is a full- or half-pool recreation time for swimmers of all ages. - Children younger than 6 or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult within arm's reach at all times. - Swimmers younger than 18 years must pass a swim test before using the deep end. - Deep water attractions may be in use: diving boards, rope swings, and water slides depending on location. - Personal Flotation Devices are available to borrow. ### Lap Swim Lap Swim is a continuous lap swim for swimmers of all ages; we divide the lanes according to speed levels. ### Early Morning Lap Swim - Exact Change or Quick Card required Early Morning Lap Swim is a great opportunity for early morning swimmers. It's for lap swimmers of all ages; we set up lanes according to speed levels. You'll need a pre-purchased swim card for entry. ## Fitness Swims ### Adult Drop In Swim Clinic Drop-In Adult Swim Stroke Clinic. Feedback provided by Red Cross Water Safety Instructors. Must have intermediate swimming ability (able to back float and comfortable in deep water). **Additional details:** Age: 16 or older Fee: Fitness Program fee applies Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ### Deep Water Exercise Deep Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a non-impact environment. Participants should be comfortable in deep water where they cannot touch the bottom. Flotation belts are provided. Deep Water Exercise incorporates aerobic conditioning, muscular strengthening, and abdominal toning. Provided resistance equipment may include dumbbell buoys and water noodles, or even just your open hands. Deep Water Exercise is often considered more advanced than Shallow Water Exercise; however, most Deep Water participants still find Shallow Water Exercise to be valuable!  ### Shallow Water Exercise Shallow Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a low-impact environment. No swimming ability is required. We recommend exercising in chest-deep water. Exercises include aerobics, strength and toning, and abdominal work.  Provided equipment may include dumbbell buoys or water noodles.  Thanks to support from the pool floor, Shallow Water Exercise may be well suited for those who want to work on balance, as well as those who may be recovering from joint injuries.*  *This is not medical advice. Please consult a qualified physician before beginning a new exercise program. ### Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout) Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout) is a structured workout led by experienced instructors designed to help you get in shape, stay in shape, or prepare for an important swim meet. Workouts are for adults 18 and older. ### Jr. Masters Jr. Masters is a drop-in competitive level coached swim for youth age 7-16 years old.  Youth should know the 4 competitive strokes and be able to swim at least 200 yards at a time. ## Special Aquatics Programs ### Adult Beginner Water Polo ($12) Adult water polo program suitable for beginners and anyone else interested in working on water polo basics in a fun environment. Topics will include strategies for passing, guarding and shooting, and each session will include a short scrimmage. Aqua Zumba is a fun twist on Shallow Water Exercise: a 45-minute, all-cardio, all-dance party led by a licensed Zumba and Aqua Zumba instructor. No swimming ability required. To account for water resistance, moves are timed more slowly than a traditional land-based Zumba class.  **Additional details:** Age: Adults, age 18+. Cost: Fitness Admission fees apply. Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round. Visit at [any swimming pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools) to get started, even when no posting is active. ## How to Apply 1. **Get Certified!** Sign up for an American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course. 2. **Get Hired**! Three options: 1. Apply online on Government Jobs, if a listing is active. 2. Send an [Aquatic Application](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/Aquatic%20Application_ADA.pdf), or resume and cover letter, to [parksaquatics@seattle.gov](mailto:parksaquatics@seattle.gov). ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.*** 3. Take your application directly to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle Parks and Recreation indoor pool. ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.*** 3. **Get Working!** Once you are hired you will be required to pass a background check and a physical examination provided by the City of Seattle, as well as take the [NW Lifeguard Test](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool#NWLifeguardTest). For more information please call [(206) 684-4078](). ## Aquatics Certifications ### Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED (American Red Cross) ## Lifeguard Training Certification All City of Seattle lifeguards must have an active **American Red Cross certification in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED.** The 30-hour blended learning course includes both online and in-person components. Completion of the course grants initial certifications in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED. **Certifications are valid for 2 years.** [Find Blended Learning - Lifeguard courses.](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20blended&viewMode=list) ### Prerequisites: - At least 15 years old on or before the final scheduled session of the course. - Swim 150 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both, maintain position at the surface of the water for 2 minutes by treading water using only the legs, then swim an additional 50 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both. Swimming on the back or side is not allowed. Swim goggles may be used. Candidates should place their hands under the armpits for the treading water portion. - Complete a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds.  Starting in the water, swim 20 yards, dive 7-10 feet to retrieve a 10 pound object, swim 20 yards on the back to return to the starting point and exit the water without using a ladder.  Swim goggles may *not* be used. --- ## Lifeguard Renewal (recertification) **Lifeguard Renewal** is a one-day course for those who have a current certification, or one that has expired in the last 30 days. It will extend the expiration date of your Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED certifications for another 2 years. [Find Lifeguard Renewal courses](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20renewal&viewMode=list) To ask about planned Lifeguard Renewal course dates later than those currently listed in our registration system, please email [parksaquatics@seattle.gov](mailto:parksaquatics@seattle.gov). ### Northwest Lifeguard Test ## Northwest Lifeguard Test The Northwest Lifeguard Test (NWLGT) is a test of swimming ability and lifeguarding skills. The test builds on skills learned in the Red Cross lifeguarding course. It is meant to be taken after completing the Red Cross lifeguarding course, and is not a substitute for Red Cross lifeguard certification. NWLGT is offered about once a month and must be taken prior to working your first shift (for permanent positions, you will have 90 days from date of hire). The test is sponsored by Seattle Parks and Recreation, King County Parks, and the City of Covington. Test elements include: 1. 50 yards head high crawl stroke* 2. Rescue tow medley and underwater swim* 3. Spinal injury rescue in shallow water 4. Submerged victim recovery and CPR 5. Rescue of struggling victim [Grading Criteria](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/NW%20test%20grading%20criteria.pdf) *There are two levels of NW Test certification. The full/beach certification, and modified/indoor pool certification. The time of the Head High 50 Yard Swim and number of breaths taken on the Underwater Swim in the Medley will determine your certification level. See Grading Criteria or call your nearest pool for details. #### 2026 Northwest Lifeguard Test Dates 1. **Sat, Feb. 7**, 1pm-5pm at [Ballard Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/ballard-pool) 2. **Sun, Mar. 8**, 8am-12pm at [Southwest Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/southwest-pool) 3. **Sat, Apr. 4**, 1pm-5pm at [Helene Madison Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/helene-madison-pool) 4. **Sun, May 3**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 5. **Sun, May 17**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 6. **Sun, June 7**, 8am-12pm at [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) 7. **Sat, June 13**, 1pm-5pm at [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) 8. **Sun, July 12**, 8am-12pm at [Meadowbrook Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/meadowbrook-pool) 9. **Sun, Aug. 16**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 10. **Sun, Nov. 15,** 8am-12pm at [Southwest Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/southwest-pool) [Register for Northwest Lifeguard Test](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?activity_keyword=northwest%20lifeguard%20test&viewMode=list) ### FREE Lifeguard Training Team (LTT) The Lifeguard Training Team is a **FREE** summer program designed to train and certify Seattle's youth in lifesaving skills. **The eight week program for youth ages 15-18** will train participants to be lifeguards and build other important job skills. Seattle Parks and Recreation provides training, books, uniforms, and basic materials at no charge. LTT participants bring their own towels, swimsuits, goggles, and snacks. The Lifeguard Training Team includes a full American Red Cross lifeguard training course, and much more! Participants get the opportunity to test for certification at the end of the program. The Lifeguard Training Team is a tremendous opportunity for you to learn and grow, to build lasting friendships, and to acquire skills you'll use for the rest of your life. You don't have to be an Olympic athlete or world class swimmer to join. We just ask that you try your hardest, participate every day, and be part of the team. The instructors' provide a safe, well supervised and encouraging environment. The safety of the participants is our #1 priority. ### 2026 LTT Program Information 50 participants max, 25 at each location. We set aside one part of the pool for lap swimming and leave the rest of the pool available for less structured swimming. ## Family Swim Family Swim is a Recreation Swim with slightly different rules to foster a somewhat quieter mood: - Children younger than 18 must be accompanied into the pool by a responsible adult. - Children younger than 6 years of age or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult who is within an arm's length at all times. ## Recreation Swim Recreation Swim is a full- or half-pool recreation time for swimmers of all ages. - Children younger than 6 or under 48" in height must be directly supervised in the water by an adult within arm's reach at all times. - Swimmers younger than 18 years must pass a swim test before using the deep end. - Deep water attractions may be in use: diving boards, rope swings, and water slides depending on location. - Personal Flotation Devices are available to borrow. ## Lap Swim Lap Swim is a continuous lap swim for swimmers of all ages; we divide the lanes according to speed levels. ## Early Morning Lap Swim - Exact Change or Quick Card required Early Morning Lap Swim is a great opportunity for early morning swimmers. It's for lap swimmers of all ages; we set up lanes according to speed levels. You'll need a pre-purchased swim card for entry. ## Fitness Swims ## Adult Drop In Swim Clinic Drop-In Adult Swim Stroke Clinic. Feedback provided by Red Cross Water Safety Instructors. Must have intermediate swimming ability (able to back float and comfortable in deep water). **Additional details:** Age: 16 or older Fee: Fitness Program fee applies Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ## Deep Water Exercise Deep Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a non-impact environment. Participants should be comfortable in deep water where they cannot touch the bottom. Flotation belts are provided. Deep Water Exercise incorporates aerobic conditioning, muscular strengthening, and abdominal toning. Provided resistance equipment may include dumbbell buoys and water noodles, or even just your open hands. Deep Water Exercise is often considered more advanced than Shallow Water Exercise; however, most Deep Water participants still find Shallow Water Exercise to be valuable!  ## Shallow Water Exercise Shallow Water Exercise is a 45-minute instructor-led class that uses water resistance in a low-impact environment. No swimming ability is required. We recommend exercising in chest-deep water. Exercises include aerobics, strength and toning, and abdominal work.  Provided equipment may include dumbbell buoys or water noodles.  Thanks to support from the pool floor, Shallow Water Exercise may be well suited for those who want to work on balance, as well as those who may be recovering from joint injuries.*  *This is not medical advice. Please consult a qualified physician before beginning a new exercise program. ## Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout) Coached Swim (formerly Masters Workout) is a structured workout led by experienced instructors designed to help you get in shape, stay in shape, or prepare for an important swim meet. Workouts are for adults 18 and older. ## Jr. Masters Jr. Masters is a drop-in competitive level coached swim for youth age 7-16 years old.  Youth should know the 4 competitive strokes and be able to swim at least 200 yards at a time. ## Special Aquatics Programs ## Adult Beginner Water Polo ($12) Adult water polo program suitable for beginners and anyone else interested in working on water polo basics in a fun environment. Topics will include strategies for passing, guarding and shooting, and each session will include a short scrimmage. To fully participate, we recommend that you feel comfortable: - Treading water for a minute with hands out of the water - Swimming 100 yards freestyle with head up **Additional details:** Age: 16 or older Fee: $12 a session Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ## Aqua Zumba Enjoy the lighter load on your joints as you dance to the Latin beats of salsa, reggaeton, merengue, and cumbia! Aqua Zumba is a fun twist on Shallow Water Exercise: a 45-minute, all-cardio, all-dance party led by a licensed Zumba and Aqua Zumba instructor. No swimming ability required. To account for water resistance, moves are timed more slowly than a traditional land-based Zumba class.  **Additional details:** Age: Adults, age 18+. Cost: Fitness Admission fees apply. Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ## Women's Only Swim (Rainier Beach only) Seattle Parks and Recreation is proud to offer single gender public swim and swimming lessons for women who, because of cultural or personal reasons, cannot swim in a co-ed environment. During these programs the windows to the pool are covered and only female instructors are employed for privacy. **Additional details:** Age: All ages. Cost: Recreation Admission fees apply. Location: [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) ## Lifeguard Jobs ## Current Aquatics Openings - **[Lifeguard (Temporary, Intermittent)](https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/seattle/jobs/5269368/lifeguard-temporary-intermittent?department%5B0%5D=Seattle%20Parks%20%26%20Recreation%20Department&sort=PositionTitle%7CAscending&pagetype=jobOpportunitiesJobs "Lifeguard Temp 2026").  Closes June 16, 2026.**  Work at swimming beaches, outdoor swimming pools, or indoor swimming pools. Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round. Visit at [any swimming pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools) to get started, even when no posting is active. ## How to Apply 1. **Get Certified!** Sign up for an American Red Cross Lifeguard Training course. 2. **Get Hired**! Three options: 1. Apply online on Government Jobs, if a listing is active. 2. Send an [Aquatic Application](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/Aquatic%20Application_ADA.pdf), or resume and cover letter, to parksaquatics@seattle.gov. ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.*** 3. Take your application directly to the Aquatic Center Coordinator at any Seattle Parks and Recreation indoor pool. ***Note, you may apply this way even if there is no GovernmentJobs.com listing.*** 3. **Get Working!** Once you are hired you will be required to pass a background check and a physical examination provided by the City of Seattle, as well as take the [NW Lifeguard Test](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/ballard-pool#NWLifeguardTest). For more information please call (206) 684-4078. ## Aquatics Certifications ## Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED (American Red Cross) ## Lifeguard Training Certification All City of Seattle lifeguards must have an active **American Red Cross certification in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED.** The 30-hour blended learning course includes both online and in-person components. Completion of the course grants initial certifications in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED. **Certifications are valid for 2 years.** [Find Blended Learning - Lifeguard courses.](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20blended&viewMode=list) ### Prerequisites: - At least 15 years old on or before the final scheduled session of the course. - Swim 150 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both, maintain position at the surface of the water for 2 minutes by treading water using only the legs, then swim an additional 50 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both. Swimming on the back or side is not allowed. Swim goggles may be used. Candidates should place their hands under the armpits for the treading water portion. - Complete a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds.  Starting in the water, swim 20 yards, dive 7-10 feet to retrieve a 10 pound object, swim 20 yards on the back to return to the starting point and exit the water without using a ladder.  Swim goggles may *not* be used. * * * ## Lifeguard Renewal (recertification) **Lifeguard Renewal** is a one-day course for those who have a current certification, or one that has expired in the last 30 days. It will extend the expiration date of your Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED certifications for another 2 years. [Find Lifeguard Renewal courses](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?onlineSiteId=0&activity_keyword=Lifeguard%20renewal&viewMode=list) To ask about planned Lifeguard Renewal course dates later than those currently listed in our registration system, please email parksaquatics@seattle.gov. ## Northwest Lifeguard Test ## Northwest Lifeguard Test The Northwest Lifeguard Test (NWLGT) is a test of swimming ability and lifeguarding skills. The test builds on skills learned in the Red Cross lifeguarding course. It is meant to be taken after completing the Red Cross lifeguarding course, and is not a substitute for Red Cross lifeguard certification. NWLGT is offered about once a month and must be taken prior to working your first shift (for permanent positions, you will have 90 days from date of hire). The test is sponsored by Seattle Parks and Recreation, King County Parks, and the City of Covington. Test elements include: 1. 50 yards head high crawl stroke* 2. Rescue tow medley and underwater swim* 3. Spinal injury rescue in shallow water 4. Submerged victim recovery and CPR 5. Rescue of struggling victim [Grading Criteria](https://seattle.gov/documents/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/NW%20test%20grading%20criteria.pdf) *There are two levels of NW Test certification. The full/beach certification, and modified/indoor pool certification. The time of the Head High 50 Yard Swim and number of breaths taken on the Underwater Swim in the Medley will determine your certification level. See Grading Criteria or call your nearest pool for details. #### 2026 Northwest Lifeguard Test Dates 01. **Sat, Feb. 7**, 1pm-5pm at [Ballard Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/ballard-pool) 02. **Sun, Mar. 8**, 8am-12pm at [Southwest Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/southwest-pool) 03. **Sat, Apr. 4**, 1pm-5pm at [Helene Madison Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/helene-madison-pool) 04. **Sun, May 3**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 05. **Sun, May 17**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 06. **Sun, June 7**, 8am-12pm at [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) 07. **Sat, June 13**, 1pm-5pm at [Rainier Beach Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/rainier-beach-pool) 08. **Sun, July 12**, 8am-12pm at [Meadowbrook Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/meadowbrook-pool) 09. **Sun, Aug. 16**, 8am-12pm at [Evans Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/evans-pool) 10. **Sun, Nov. 15,** 8am-12pm at [Southwest Pool](https://seattle.gov/parks/pools/southwest-pool) [Register for Northwest Lifeguard Test](https://anc.apm.activecommunities.com/seattle/activity/search?activity_keyword=northwest%20lifeguard%20test&viewMode=list) ## FREE Lifeguard Training Team (LTT) The Lifeguard Training Team is a **FREE** summer program designed to train and certify Seattle's youth in lifesaving skills. **The eight week program for youth ages 15-18** will train participants to be lifeguards and build other important job skills. Seattle Parks and Recreation provides training, books, uniforms, and basic materials at no charge. LTT participants bring their own towels, swimsuits, goggles, and snacks. The Lifeguard Training Team includes a full American Red Cross lifeguard training course, and much more! Participants get the opportunity to test for certification at the end of the program. The Lifeguard Training Team is a tremendous opportunity for you to learn and grow, to build lasting friendships, and to acquire skills you'll use for the rest of your life. You don't have to be an Olympic athlete or world class swimmer to join. We just ask that you try your hardest, participate every day, and be part of the team. The instructors' provide a safe, well supervised and encouraging environment. The safety of the participants is our #1 priority. ### 2026 LTT Program Information 50 participants max, 25 at each location. Full attendance is mandatory. Participants must pass the lifeguard pre-test. Early registration is encouraged as LTT fills on a first-come, first served basis.  June 29 - August 20, 2026. Monday - Thursday, 1pm - 5pm South location: Pritchard Beach, [8400 55th Ave S, 98118](https://www.google.com/maps/place/8400+55th+Ave+S,+Seattle,+WA+98118/@47.5298267,-122.266172,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x5490420a71f550e9:0x54145e7fa1ceb76b!8m2!3d47.5298231!4d-122.2635971!16s%2Fg%2F11cnd8q08l!5m1!1e1?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDQxNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) North location: West Green Lake Beach [7312 W Green Lake Dr N, 98103](https://www.google.com/maps/place/7312+West+Green+Lake+Dr+N,+Seattle,+WA+98103/@47.6821168,-122.3423875,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x54901415e801e2b5:0xb88d5214d8912e10!8m2!3d47.6821132!4d-122.3398126!16s%2Fg%2F11c3q4947v!5m1!1e1?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDQxNS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D) ### Participant Swimming Skills Pre-Test Each participant must attend a swimming skills pre-tests before the first class. The pre-test is a prerequisite for the American Red Cross Lifeguard Training Course. It is also your chance to meet the instructors and ask questions about the program. Please bring a swimsuit and towel and be prepared to swim. **Pre-tests will take place at indoor pools in June, and take about 1 hour.** Specific date and location options will be provided when applications are accepted. ### Prerequisites: - Swim 150 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both, maintain position at the surface of the water for 2 minutes by treading water using only the legs, then swim an additional 50 yards using the front crawl, breaststroke or a combination of both. Swimming on the back or side is not allowed. Swim goggles may be used. Candidates should place their hands under the armpits for the treading water portion. - Complete a timed event within 1 minute, 40 seconds.  Starting in the water, swim 20 yards, dive 7-10 feet to retrieve a 10 pound object, swim 20 yards on the back to return to the starting point and exit the water without using a ladder.  Swim goggles may *not* be used. [Apply for the Lifeguard Training Team!](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=RR7meOtrCUCPmTWdi1T0G_X1kIYNvm9AinyqLpWJsfRUME03UUJHSVNYN01KVUhJVkJHQVI5QVc1VS4u) ## Sr. Lifeguard: Water Safety Instructor, Lifeguard Instructor ## Water Safety Instructor (WSI) Senior Lifeguards are required to hold a [Water Safety Instructor](https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/swimming/water-safety/water-safety-instructor-certification) certification from the American Red Cross.  The certification may be attained within 90 days of hire. ## Lifeguard Instructor (LGI) This approximately 30 hour course includes practical methods and theory for teaching lifeguarding skills. Candidates must have a current Red Cross certification in Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED. LGI-certified instructors can certify in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR/AED. Completion of this course also extends your Lifeguard, First Aid, and CPR/AED certifications for 2 years. Lifeguard Instructor is a highly desired, but optional certification for Senior Lifeguards. LGI is required for Assistant Aquatic Center Coordinator and Aquatic Center Coordinator positions. ## Amenities - Rope Swing - 1 M Diving Board - Exercise Equipment - Water Slide - Spa/warm pool - Family changing rooms - ADA Lift - Portable Access Stairs ## Images [ ](https://seattle.gov/images//images/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/BallardPool/BallardPool1.jpg) [ ](https://seattle.gov/images//images/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/BallardPool/BallardPool7.jpg) [ ](https://seattle.gov/images//images/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/BallardPool/BallardPool3.jpg) [ ](https://seattle.gov/images//images/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/BallardPool/BallardPool4.jpg) [ ](https://seattle.gov/images//images/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/BallardPool/BallardPool5.jpg) [ ](https://seattle.gov/images//images/Departments/ParksAndRecreation/Swimming/BallardPool/BallardPool6.jpg) ## About Located in the heart of Ballard, we offer a wide array of aquatics programs for all ages. Our 25-yard, 6-lane pool is heated to 85 degrees. Lessons include parent & child lessons (6 months to 4 years of age), preschool lessons, youth lessons, youth competitive stroke lessons, adult and senior adult lessons, and private lessons. We offer exercise classes including aqua jogging, hyrdofit exercise, and water exercise.
